title: A constants file
idea: A constants file is one module that holds fixed values, such as role names and the database name, so every file imports the same spelling.
points: `src/constants.js` exports each value once; other files import it by name.
`UserRolesEnum` is an enum: a fixed set of named values, here role strings.
`Object.values` builds `AvailableUserRoles` from the enum, so the two cannot drift apart.
`Object.freeze` makes the enum read-only; a `const` alone would not.

left.title: The same string in many files
items: Renaming a role means searching every file

right.title: One constants file
items: `AvailableUserRoles` is a ready list to check against
Renaming a role is one edit

code.title: src/constants.js
code.caption: Lines 1-3 are `src/constants.js`. The rest plays another file that imports them.

walk.text: Keys are readable names, values are the strings you store. `freeze` locks the object.
`Object.values` lists the role strings, so a new role is added in one place.
The database name is not a secret, so it can live in code.
A caller checks a value against the list. `includes` needs the exact string, so `'Admin'` fails.
Print the list and the database name.
Inside a module, assigning to a frozen property throws a `TypeError`.
A misspelled key is not an error: you get `undefined`.

pitfalls: `const` blocks reassignment, not edits to properties; freeze enum objects.
A misspelled key such as `UserRolesEnum.ADMN` is `undefined`, not an error.
Keep secrets and per-machine values, such as `MONGO_URI`, in `.env`, not here.

quiz.why: `Object.values` returns the values, `'admin'` and `'user'`. `'ADMIN'` is a key, so `includes` is false.

takeaway: Define fixed values once, freeze them, and import them everywhere.

starters: When does a value belong in `.env` instead of `constants.js`?
